findings.evidence: roadmap/TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/README.md:70-77 'Scalar ℂ throughout the conformal layers (L0–L6) … every theorem this entry adds … is scalar ℂ'; README:102,151 lists Montel/normal-families/Vitali as content this entry adds; diff generalises TauCeti.montel, TauCeti.vitali, TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn, TauCeti.isCompact_closure_range_of_isLocallyBoundedOn.
findings.fix: Keep the L1 chain at scalar ℂ as the roadmap fixes. If Banach-valued Montel is wanted, a human must first amend ConformalMapping/README.md's generality bar; land the generalisation only after that.
findings.issue: Generalising TauCeti.montel / vitali / IsLocallyBoundedOn / isCompact_closure_range_* to an arbitrary (proper) complex normed space E exceeds the roadmap's explicit generality bar, which states scalar ℂ for every theorem this entry adds across L0–L6. These declarations are L1 content this entry adds (README lists Montel/Vitali as 'the unique content of this entry'), not Mathlib inputs, so the bar governs them. No roadmap target consumes Banach-valued normal families — RMT is scalar, Schwarz reflection has 'no Banach-E analogue' — so the added generality has no path to a target.

summary: The PR generalises TauCeti's own L1 normal-families theorems (montel, vitali, IsLocallyBoundedOn, precompactness) from scalar ℂ to Banach-valued E, but the conformal-mapping roadmap's generality bar deliberately fixes scalar ℂ for every theorem this entry adds (L0–L6), and no roadmap target needs the E-valued generality. This is off-roadmap over-generalisation against an explicit up-front decision; a human must relax the bar first.
